——If possible, it would be better if no one had to grieve.

If a little help from someone like me is enough to make the people around me happy, then the world must be a wonderfully easy place to live.

The man who was a Hero of Justice to me claimed that, by his own reckoning, he was only a washout who had failed to become one.

The man who was a superhero to me was saying that he thought he was a failure.

pages.en:
It needed no explanation.

The world I knew as a child and the world Kiritsugu knew as an adult were too different. We had different ideas of the passing mark for a Hero of Justice.

As a child, this house was my entire world.

It would have been enough for me to protect my old man, Kiritsugu, Fuji, myself, and the storehouse I loved, forever.
pages.mirrorMoon:
He didn’t even need to explain it to me.
The world of the young me was so different from the world of the adult Kiritsugu that the passing grade to be a superhero was different.
For me as a child, the house was my only world.
So it was enough for me if I could keep protecting my father, Fuji-nee, myself, and the shed that I loved.

Some will always remain beyond salvation.

No one can save them all.

If reaching for one thousand means letting five hundred slip through your fingers——

Then abandon one hundred, and save the other nine hundred to the last.

That is the finest method available.

The ideal method, Kiritsugu once muttered, and only once.

It is impossible to save everyone.
If I have to lose five hundred to earn one thousand,
I will abandon one hundred and save the lives of nine hundred.
That is the most efficient method.

Even if it was idealism, even if it was an impossible dream, a Hero of Justice was someone who tried to make it real.

I turn away from the two of them with a huff and shovel down my meal.

…Then——

“Why go to all that pointless trouble?”

Fuji, who has been watching my exchange with Tohsaka in puzzlement, murmurs the question absently.

I look away from the two with a humph and start eating.
…And then.
“Why are you doing something so pointless?”
Fuji-nee, who has watched our conversation with wonder, murmurs.

Fuji-nee eats after nodding that it’s a problem.
“……”
…No.
I have to come up with some countermeasure real soon or I’ll really lose my position…

“T-That’s right, Shirou. There’s nothing wrong with you to make you skip school, right?”
“No, my wound hurts. Old wounds hurt when the temperature goes down, right? It’s kind of like that.”
